content.title: SIGNS YOU'RE ACTUALLY {{HEALTHIER}} THAN YOU THINK
facts: **Sneezing twice in a row** -> your nasal reflex is extra sensitive, clearing irritants fast before they reach your lungs
**Loud stomach growling** -> your migrating motor complex is sweeping leftover debris through your gut between meals
**Waking up thirsty** -> your kidneys are doing a precise overnight job concentrating urine instead of wasting water
**Goosebumps during music** -> a strong dopamine response, linked to a brain that processes emotion vividly
**Sighing often** -> your lungs are resetting collapsed air sacs, a built-in breathing reflex that keeps them flexible
**Cold hands after a hot shower** -> healthy blood vessels rapidly redirecting flow to your core to regulate temperature
**Vivid, strange dreams** -> deep REM sleep, the stage tied to memory consolidation and emotional processing
**Catching a cold once a year** -> your immune system actively sampling and learning from new pathogens, not a weak one
**Sweating fast during a workout** -> a well-trained cooling system that kicks in early instead of overheating

content.caption:
A few of these deserve more explaining. That stomach growling (borborygmi, technically) happens because of the migrating motor complex, a wave of muscle contractions that sweeps through your gut every 90-120 minutes between meals to clear out leftover food and bacteria - hearing it often is a sign that cleanup crew is working on schedule. Waking up thirsty is your kidneys finishing an overnight job: while you sleep, antidiuretic hormone rises so your kidneys concentrate urine and conserve water, and thirst on waking just means that system handed control back to you smoothly. And those vivid dreams come from spending solid time in REM sleep, the stage where your brain replays and files away the day's emotional information - the weirder the dream, the more actively that filing is happening. Everyone's body is different, listen to yours.

This is the kind of everyday body-literacy we focus on at @smarthealthfix, covering nutrition, common symptoms, organ function, and the small daily habits that quietly shape your health. Our mission is to help you feel less alarmed by normal signals and more in tune with what your body is actually telling you.
